checked_sources.title: Fully Dynamic Matching in Bipartite Graphs
source_observations: The EDCS definition uses P1: every used edge has endpoint-degree sum <= beta.
The EDCS definition uses P2: every unused graph edge has endpoint-degree sum >= beta_minus.
The dynamic maintenance algorithm uses alternating full/augmentable paths and orientation/bucket information updates.
The paper states that the EDCS structure has a global effect even though the constraints are local, and the maintenance algorithm explicitly restores P1/P2 after updates.
The theorem gives parameterized matching guarantees for a valid EDCS; it does not validate the lazy one-repair variant defined in this experiment.

checked_sources.title: Deterministic Dynamic Matching In Worst-Case Update Time
source_observations: The paper studies deterministic dynamic matching with explicit approximation and worst-case update-time guarantees.
Its result is not an evaluation of the lazy repair rule tested here and is used only as a prior-art boundary for dynamic matching guarantees.

variant_boundary.tested_object: A deterministic one-repair-per-external-update EDCS-like maintenance rule defined in research/edcs_experiment_protocol_v1.json.
variant_boundary.interpretation_rule: A failure is evidence against this frozen variant under the finite tested boundary only; it is not a counterexample to the original EDCS definition, theorem or Bernstein-Stein maintenance algorithm. No failure is not a proof.
